newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African rand undervalued - UBS.
newsitem.headline: South African rand undervalued - UBS.

text.p: A sharp rise in South Africa's trade surplus suggests the rand will appreciate strongly in real terms in 1997, after allowing for inflation differentials, Union Bank of Switzerland said in its latest Currency Focus report.
"On the basis of the rising trade surplus and the real interest rates, we continue to forecast USD/ZAR at 4.8500 at year-end," the bank said. "This is below the forward exchange rate of 5.0900.
On a trade-weighted basis, UBS said that current dollar/Deutschmark and dollar/sterling rates suggested the currency's equilibrium was closer to 4.15 against the dollar.
"There is no way that USD/ZAR can remain above 4.60. Equilibrium is closer to 4.15," it said.

South Africa recorded a trade surplus of 2.040 billion rand in December from a 378 million rand surplus in November. This brought the country's year surplus to 10.577 billion rand against 4.884 billion in 1995.
UBS noted that in the 10 months since the rand's devaluation last year, the trade surplus had risen to 10.046 billion rand from 264 million rand in the same period in 1995.

The latest UBS report comes a year after the bank issued a report stating that the rand was overvalued, which analysts then pointed to as one of the triggers for the rand's 30 percent slide against the dollar last year.
Some traders cited the latest report as a factor which helped the rand to its strongest level in two months against the dollar on Monday.
The currency touched 4.5940 bid against the dollar earlier in the morning, a level last seen on November 29 last year.
